content.text:
## Root cause

`cmd /c start` was handing the OAuth URL to **cmd.exe, which treats an unquoted `&` as a command separator**. The URL was truncated at the first `&`.

`cmd/entire/cli/login.go:536` (as shipped in v0.10.0 — I confirmed via `git show v0.10.0`):

```go
case "windows":
    command = "cmd"
    args = []string{"/c", "start", "", browserURL}
```

Go's escaping doesn't save you here: `syscall.EscapeArg` only quotes an argument containing a space, tab, quote, or backslash. A URL has none of those, so it reaches cmd.exe bare.

The authorize URL is built with `url.Values.Encode()`, which sorts keys — so `client_id` comes first and `redirect_uri` sits behind three `&`s:

```
…/authorize?client_id=entire-cli&code_challenge=…&code_challenge_method=S256&redirect_uri=…
                                ^ cmd.exe cuts here
```

Leaving exactly `https://us.auth.entire.io/authorize?client_id=entire-cli` — byte-for-byte what your user reported, hence "missing redirect uri". Only the default browser flow is affected; `--device` isn't (see below).

It's macOS/Linux-only-tested code that's been broken since Mar 2026 (`5c44ffb87`), and only became user-visible when the browser redirect became the default login.

## Immediate workaround for the user

```
entire login --device
```

I verified against the live endpoint that its URL is `https://us.auth.entire.io/cli/auth?user_code=XXXX-XXXX` — a single query param, no `&`, so it survives cmd.exe intact. The device flow also prints the URL unconditionally, so copy-paste always works.

## Fix

Split the launcher per platform and, on Windows, call the Win32 `ShellExecute` API directly — no command line, so nothing to parse or escape. This is what `github.com/pkg/browser` switched to, and `golang.org/x/sys` was already a direct dependency.

- `cmd/entire/cli/browser_open_windows.go` (new) — `ShellExecute` via a `shellExecute` seam for testing
- `cmd/entire/cli/browser_open_other.go` (new) — `open`/`xdg-open`, unchanged behavior
- `cmd/entire/cli/login.go` — `openBrowser` keeps URL validation and the under-test guard, then delegates

Quoting alone wouldn't have been enough: the percent-encoded `redirect_uri` also exposes the URL to cmd's `%VAR%` expansion.

Tests: `browser_open_windows_test.go` asserts the whole URL reaches the shell association, plus a second test that executes `cmd /c echo <url>` to pin the truncation as the root cause so nobody reintroduces the shell. Both have `Windows` in the name, so the existing `test-windows` CI job (`-run '(Windows|MSYS)'`) picks them up. `browser_open_test.go` covers scheme validation cross-platform.

Verified: builds for darwin/windows/linux, `golangci-lint` clean on both darwin and `GOOS=windows` (the default run skips `_windows.go` files), and `mise run test:ci` passed. The Windows tests compile for windows/amd64 but I couldn't execute them here — they'll run on the CI Windows job.

## One thing worth deciding separately

`runBrowserLogin` (`login.go:289`) only prints the full URL when `openURL` returns an error. The truncated launch *succeeded* from our side, so the user got no copy-paste fallback — dead end. A successful browser spawn isn't proof the browser got a usable URL. I left that as-is since it's outside this bug, but printing the URL unconditionally (as the device flow does) would have made this self-service.

#### Invoking Commands on Windows - Never Put a Dynamic Value on a cmd.exe Line

**When Entire performs the exec itself, do not go through `cmd.exe`.** Pass the
program and its arguments as separate argv elements (`exec.Command(prog, arg)`),
or call the Win32 API directly.

cmd.exe treats `&`, `|`, `<`, `>` as command separators/redirections and expands
`%VAR%`, and **Go's argv escaping will not protect you**: `syscall.EscapeArg`
only quotes an argument containing a space, tab, quote, or backslash. A URL,
a percent-encoded path, or any `&`-bearing string therefore reaches cmd.exe bare
and is silently cut at the first metacharacter. That is exactly how
`entire login` shipped a Windows build that opened
`…/authorize?client_id=entire-cli` and got rejected for a missing
`redirect_uri` — the `cmd /c start "" <url>` launcher lost everything from the
first `&` on, and because the truncation happened inside the released child, the
CLI saw a successful launch and printed no fallback URL.

Escaping is the right tool in exactly one situation: **a third party owns the
exec.** When Entire writes a command into an agent's config file (Cursor/Codex
`hooks.json`) and that agent runs it through cmd.exe, there is no shell to
avoid — use `agent.escapeWindowsCMD`. Reviewers should flag any new
`exec.Command("cmd", …)` / `"cmd.exe"` call site that interpolates a
non-constant value.

avoid-the-shell side) and `cmd/entire/cli/agent/hook_command.go`

## The bug

A user on Windows running v0.10.0 reported that `entire login` opens

```
https://us.auth.entire.io/authorize?client_id=entire-cli
```

and the authorization server rejects it with **"auth request is missing redirect uri"**.

## Root cause

`openBrowser` launched the URL through cmd.exe:

```go
case "windows":
    command = "cmd"
    args = []string{"/c", "start", "", browserURL}
```

cmd.exe treats an unquoted `&` as a command separator, so the browser only ever received the text before the first `&`.

Go's argv escaping does not help here: `syscall.EscapeArg` only quotes an argument containing a space, tab, quote, or backslash, and a URL has none of those, so it reaches cmd.exe bare. Because `url.Values.Encode` sorts keys, `client_id` sorts first and `redirect_uri` sits behind three separators.

Here is a real authorization URL from the production auth server:

```
…/authorize?client_id=entire-cli&code_challenge=UwBw-uNt…&code_challenge_method=S256&redirect_uri=http%3A%2F%2F127.0.0.1%3A59656%2Fcallback&response_type=code&scope=cli+offline_access&state=moEAbe7a…
                                ^ cmd.exe cuts here
```

Everything from `code_challenge` on is lost, leaving `…/authorize?client_id=entire-cli` — byte-for-byte the URL in the report.

Quoting alone would not have been enough either — the percent-encoded `redirect_uri` also exposes the URL to cmd's `%VAR%` expansion.

Broken since 5c44ffb87 (Mar 2026), but only user-visible once the browser redirect became the default login flow.

## Workaround for affected users, until this ships

```
entire login --device
```

Captured from a real run:

```
Device code: BN5V-FV8V
Login URL:   https://us.auth.entire.io/cli/auth?user_code=BN5V-FV8V

Waiting for approval...
```

Two reasons this is immune:

1. **One query parameter, no `&`** — there is nothing for cmd.exe to cut, so the browser receives the whole URL. Verified against the live `/device_authorization` endpoint.
2. **The URL is printed unconditionally**, before any browser launch, so copy-paste works even if the open misbehaves.

Approval then polls over HTTPS with no shell involved. Nothing is degraded relative to the redirect flow.

<details>
<summary>Second option, if the redirect flow is specifically needed</summary>

`ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=1 entire login` makes the browser open fail deliberately, so the CLI prints the full authorization URL and keeps the loopback listener waiting — paste it into a browser and the login completes on the redirect flow. (This is how the real URL above was captured.)

Hold this in reserve rather than recommending it: `ENTIRE_TEST_TTY` is an internal test switch, not a supported user-facing knob, and it also suppresses the Enter prompt as a side effect.

</details>

## The fix

Split the launcher per platform and, on Windows, call the Win32 `ShellExecute` API directly (as `github.com/pkg/browser` does) so the URL is passed as a single wide string — no command line to parse, nothing to escape. `golang.org/x/sys` was already a direct dependency, and already in the Windows import graph, so this costs +1,024 bytes of PE page rounding.

- `browser_open_windows.go` (new) — `ShellExecute`, behind a `shellExecute` var so tests can capture the string without launching a browser
- `browser_open_other.go` (new) — `open` / `xdg-open`; these never involved a shell
- `login.go` — `openBrowser` keeps URL validation and the under-test guard, then delegates to `openBrowserPlatform`

The second commit is a cleanup pass. Two things in it are worth calling out:

**A goroutine leak, carried over verbatim from the old launcher.** `exec.CommandContext` sets `Cmd.Cancel`, so `Start` spawns a `watchCtx` goroutine whose result channel only `Wait` drains — and this path deliberately never calls `Wait`. Every browser open leaked one goroutine, retaining the `Cmd` (argv, env, URL), for the process lifetime. Measured: 20 opens leaked 20 goroutines, surviving both cancel and GC; with `exec.Command` it is zero. The context was already inert here because `Process.Release` detaches the child, so `Cmd.Cancel`'s `Process.Kill` fails regardless — dropping it removes the leak without losing cancellation that ever worked. Bounded for `login`, but `experts --tui` is long-lived and opens several links.

**Naming the boundary between this repo's two Windows-command philosophies**, which previously discussed the same hazard from opposite sides without referencing each other. The split turns on *who owns the exec*: escape when a third party runs your command (`agent.escapeWindowsCMD`, for agents' `hooks.json`), bypass the shell when Entire launches it itself. Reciprocal doc pointers, plus a `CLAUDE.md` section under Code Patterns recording the invariant and the `EscapeArg` fact that made the bug possible.

## Tests

`TestOpenBrowserWindows_PassesWholeURLToShellAssociation`, named so the existing `test-windows` CI job picks it up (it selects `-run '(Windows|MSYS)'`): the whole URL, `&` separators and percent-encoding intact, reaches the shell association. Reintroducing a shell launcher stops the seam being called and fails this test.

Plus `browser_open_test.go` covering URL validation cross-platform.

An earlier revision also had a test asserting that `cmd /c echo <url>` truncates at the first `&`. It was dropped in the cleanup commit: it called no code from this repo, so it passed identically whether the launcher used `ShellExecute` or `cmd /c start`, and could not detect the regression it claimed to guard — while costing a cmd.exe process plus six failed PATH×PATHEXT resolutions on every Windows CI run.

Verified: builds for darwin/windows/linux; `golangci-lint` clean on both darwin and `GOOS=windows` (the default run skips `_windows.go` files); `mise run test:ci` passes. The Windows test compiles for windows/amd64 but was not executed locally — it runs in CI.

## Scope

`openBrowser` has two production callers and both are covered: `login.go` (browser and `--device` flows) and `experts_tui.go` via `openExpertsSessionCmd`. The experts session URL is path-only (`url.PathEscape`, no query string), so it had no `&` and was not affected by this bug — it just becomes robust for free.

This is the whole population of the bug class. The repo's only other cmd.exe call sites — `versioncheck/autoupdate.go` and the `agent/hook_command.go` wrappers — interpolate compile-time constants only, and the one genuinely variable value there already goes through `escapeWindowsCMD`.

## Deliberately not addressed

`runBrowserLogin` only prints the full URL when the browser open *reports failure*. This launch succeeded from our side while delivering a mangled URL, so the user had no copy-paste fallback and was fully stuck. Printing the URL unconditionally (as the device flow does) would make this class of failure self-service, but that is a separate behavior change.

What *would* flip it between two runs: `CI` set in the environment, output piped or redirected rather than going to a console, or launching via WinRM/PsExec/SSH instead of an interactive session.

## A hypothesis that explains everything, including why your colleague disagrees

`/dev/tty` on Windows resolves drive-root-relative — to **`C:\dev\tty`**. If that path happens to exist on the reporter's machine, the probe opens it, `ttyInRawMode` returns false on Windows (`rawmode_other.go`), so `canPrompt` comes back **true** and they get the browser flow. A clean VM has no `C:\dev`, so the probe fails and your colleague gets the device flow.

That reconciles all three observations without needing a shell difference:

- Colleague, clean VM → device flow. Correct.
- Reporter, dev machine with a stray `C:\dev\tty` → browser flow → `&`-bearing authorize URL → cmd.exe truncation → their exact error. Correct.
- Same binary, same code, different outcome.

A `C:\dev` is the sort of thing POSIX-emulation tooling leaves behind, which fits someone with a heavily-tooled Windows box.

Ask the reporter, in PowerShell:

```powershell
Test-Path C:\dev\tty; Test-Path C:\dev; $env:CI; $env:ENTIRE_TEST_TTY
```

content.text:
Conflicts resolved and pushed. PR #1981 is now `MERGEABLE` (`BLOCKED` is just pending checks/review, not a conflict).

## The conflict

One file: `cmd/entire/cli/login.go`. Main had moved 94 commits ahead and landed an **interactive login-URL prompt** — `loginURLInteractor`, `readLoginURLAction`, and a Bubble Tea `loginURLActionModel` — inserted immediately above `openBrowser`, while this branch had rewritten `openBrowser`'s doc comment and dropped its unused context parameter. Adjacent edits, not competing ones.

Resolution: kept main's new block verbatim, then this branch's `openBrowser`. Two details worth noting:

- The function **body** merged cleanly to `return openBrowserPlatform(browserURL)` — the ShellExecute delegation survived untouched.
- Main had also shortened the under-test comment inside the body, and git took that version. That's the right outcome, not a loss: main shortened it precisely because the old rationale ("so the caller takes the here's-the-URL fallback") no longer describes how the code works.

I used a merge rather than a rebase so your colleague's checkout of the branch doesn't get invalidated by a force-push.

## Something main changed that affects our open questions

`runBrowserLogin` now prints the login URL **unconditionally** (`login.go:350`), before any browser launch, and opening the browser is an explicit keypress with a copy-to-clipboard option:

```go
fmt.Fprintf(outW, "Logging in to %s\n\n", baseURL)
printLoginURL(outW, browserLoginURLLabel, authURL)
```

So the hardening I'd been recommending landed on main independently — that decision is off the table. It also means the specific dead end your reporter hit is already gone on main: they'd now see the full URL and could copy it even with the truncating launcher. The ShellExecute fix still matters, because pressing Enter should open a URL that works.

Verified on the merged tree: builds for darwin/windows/linux, Windows test binary compiles, `mise run lint` clean plus a `GOOS=windows` pass, and `mise run test:ci` green. Net diff versus main is still exactly our 7 files (+210/−30) — the merge pulled in no collateral.

One thing that tripped me up in case you hit it: `mise run lint` fails mid-merge with *"go module files modified, please commit result of go mod tidy"*. That's a false positive — `lint:gomod` uses `git status --porcelain`, which also reports staged changes, and the merge legitimately stages main's `go.mod`. `go mod tidy` had made no changes of its own; it passes once the merge is committed.

The `/dev/tty`-on-Windows question is still open and still worth settling — say the word and I'll put up that CI probe.
